page: Amazon Web Services i3.xlarge is a storage-optimized instance running on the Xen hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2686 v4 processor. This dedicated CPU configuration provides 4 vCPUs across 2 physical cores with hyper-threading operating at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz. The processor includes a 45 MB L3 cache and supports AVX, AES, and FMA instruction sets, though it lacks AVX-512 extensions. The instance is equipped with 30.0 GB of system memory, translating to 7.62 GB per core, and includes a bundled 950 GB NVMe SSD for high-capacity local storage. Baseline network bandwidth is rated at 1 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate that the i3.xlarge exhibits modest computational and memory performance. In stress-ng testing, single-core CPU performance registered at 883.17 and multi-core at 2080.35, placing both in the lower tier of tested hardware. Memory bandwidth tests showed 157.88 GB/sec for cached small-block reads, but dropped to 22.62 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 14.23 GB/sec for large-block writes. Geekbench scores align with these findings, yielding a single-core score of 898.0 and a multi-core score of 1900.0. Database operations, such as Redis SET, achieved 2.54 million operations per second, while static web serving throughput reached 2.81 GB/sec.

The primary value proposition of the i3.xlarge lies in its storage density rather than raw processing power. The inclusion of a 950 GB NVMe SSD provides substantial local storage capacity, but the underlying Intel Xeon E5-2686 v4 processor and memory subsystem present performance bottlenecks for compute-heavy workloads. Consequently, this instance is best suited for storage-centric applications that require high local capacity but have moderate CPU demands, such as NoSQL databases, transactional data stores, and distributed file systems, rather than intensive data science, large-scale compilation, or high-throughput web serving.
description: Amazon Web Services i3.xlarge is a storage-optimized instance designed for workloads requiring significant local storage capacity. Powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2686 v4 processor on the x86_64 architecture, it provides 4 dedicated vCPUs, 30.0 GB of system memory, and a bundled 950 GB NVMe SSD. Running on the Xen hypervisor, the instance delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps. Benchmark data reveals modest computational capabilities, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 1900.0 and a stress-ng multi-core score of 2080.35. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, recording 22.62 GB/sec for large-block reads. Given these performance characteristics, the i3.xlarge represents a qualitative tradeoff, offering high local storage density at the expense of raw processing and memory throughput. It is best suited for storage-intensive applications with moderate CPU requirements, such as local database hosting and distributed file systems.
